meta.unit: prices poller acquisition + chain pinned call
meta.purpose: Task 9 wave 1 brief's mutation requirement: every NEW guard arm of the endpoint-coherent, block-pinned readRound recomposition, plus the additive chain.Failover.CallAtFrom's pin and routing discipline, each stating the property it certifies. Run through the wave-16 committed applier (.superpowers/sdd/wave16-mutations/mutate.py) per the wave-16 class rule.
meta.equivalent_mutants_excluded: Two candidate mutations are equivalent post-guard and carry no row: (a) stamping observations with the multicall's returned block instead of the pin — the blockNumber==pin guard makes them identical wherever a round survives to stamp anything; (b) anchoring to hashAfter instead of hashBefore — the hashAfter==hashBefore guard makes them identical wherever a round survives to anchor. Killing either would require first killing the guard that makes them equivalent, which M2/M3 already attack directly.
meta.not_mutation_testable: The comment sweep (package comment, multicall3ABI doc, unpackMulticallResult doc, routing comments no longer claiming the multicall supplies the anchor hash) is prose; no mutation of a comment can fail a test, so it carries no row and is not reported as covered. The explore-over-pin routing PRECEDENCE inside readRound predates this wave (carried over verbatim from the old switch) and is not a new guard arm; it carries no row either.
meta.test_env: TEST_DATABASE_URL exported (solvent_t9w1, the wave's dedicated DB — never the running daemon's) so the live-store test runs rather than skips; packages are run whole so a kill is attributed to the tests that actually failed, not to a -run filter chosen to make one fail.

mutations.description: the multicall decoder refuses the zero blockHash again (the live P0 restored)
mutations.property: the real-EVM zero multicall hash decodes cleanly — tryBlockAndAggregate's blockHash is blockhash(block.number), out of BLOCKHASH range, deterministically zero on every real chain; refusing it refuses every round on every real chain
a multicall that reports executing at a different height than the block it was pinned to (a serving inconsistency behind one URL) can never land: the round is discarded, nothing is applied

a mid-round reorg — the header hash at the pin changing between the two reads that bracket the multicall — discards the round: no anchor is ever written for a block the serving endpoint no longer carries

mutations.description: the multicall endpoint-coherence check is disabled
mutations.property: a pinned multicall the failover client served from a DIFFERENT endpoint than the round's own is another chain view's answer and discards the round — one endpoint serves every read, or nothing lands

mutations.description: the closing re-read's endpoint-coherence check is disabled
mutations.property: a closing HeaderHash(N) re-read answered by another endpoint cannot confirm the round's own chain view and discards the round — a second node agreeing on a hash is a different fact than one node bracketing its own answer

mutations.description: the zero-hash refusal on the OPENING header read is disabled
mutations.property: a zero header hash is a provider protocol violation and is refused BEFORE any multicall is issued — the guard that used to sit (wrongly) in the multicall decoder now protects the hash the anchor actually rests on
mutations.note: The before-arm test's load-bearing assertion is require.Empty(ch.calls): under this mutant the round proceeds to the multicall and may still error later for a different reason, so the refusal's POSITION (before any RPC spend) is part of the property.

mutations.description: the zero-hash refusal on the CLOSING header read is disabled
mutations.property: a zero header hash on the closing read is an ERROR (a broken provider, operator-visible as a fault), never a silent discard-and-retry

mutations.description: Step treats a discarded round as landed
mutations.property: a discarded round records NOTHING: Step's discard arm is what stands between an incoherent round and ApplyPolledPrices — removing it must be caught by every discard test's 'nothing reached the store' assertion

mutations.description: the anchor's hash is zeroed at Step's composition site
mutations.property: the durable anchor persists the round's verified header hash — the exact bytes HeaderHash(N) attested on both sides of the multicall — not a placeholder

mutations.description: the multicall is pinned one block past the resolved head
mutations.property: the multicall executes AT the pin the round verified — the pinned height and the header-verified height are the same N, or the anchor describes a block nobody read

mutations.description: the default endpoint resolution ignores the shared routing hint
mutations.property: with no exploration hint and no attribution pin, the round resolves from the endpoint the shared hint names (read, never written) — not from a hard-coded index

mutations.description: chain.Failover.CallAtFrom silently drops its pin to latest
mutations.property: the pin is forwarded to eth_call: a CallAtFrom that executes at 'latest' is indistinguishable from Call at the RPC layer and would reintroduce the unverifiable-round defect one layer down
